header: I do not let a department the question names but nobody can find turn into "everybody" (step 44d). The older rule-based engine (the omnibar's safety net when the model's attempt fails) drops a department phrase it does not know and answers for the whole plant: "how many executives are there in heavy maintenance, list them?" was answered "DSP currently has 1,169 executives." with the executives of every department listed: a confident wrong answer. Since 29 Sep 2026 that engine deliberately no longer reports "I couldn't identify the department X" for leftover text (phrases such as "at any position" were misfiring), so I close the gap here, narrowly: ONLY the engine's unscoped company-wide count is checked, and only against a phrase after in / at / under / within / inside / from that is not generic wording ("the plant", "DSP", "each department", "grade E-5", "total").

symbols.name: unresolvedDepartmentPhrase
symbols.sig: export function unresolvedDepartmentPhrase(q: string): string | null
doc: I take the department-like phrase after in / at / under / within / inside / from; null when the question has none (or only generic wording).

symbols.name: withoutBlindScope
symbols.sig: export function withoutBlindScope(q: string, p: AnalyticsPayload | null): AnalyticsPayload | null
doc: I return the older engine's answer unchanged, unless it is the unscoped company-wide count ("DSP currently has N executives.") to a question that names a department it could not find: then the person gets an honest question instead of a wrong number. Any other answer (a department's own count, a list by name, a breakdown, a holiday) is returned as it is.

behaviours: the company-wide count for a question that names an unknown department becomes an honest question
...and carries no count and no people
a designation count for an unknown department is blocked too
